title: The impact of an intensified outpatient prehabilitation program during neoadjuvant therapy on postoperative outcomes and convalescence in visceral oncology patients.
summary: Unter neoadjuvanter Therapie weisen Patienten häufig einen Verlust an funktioneller Organreserve auf (u. a. in Form einer Sarkopenie), was unmittelbar mit einer erhöhten postoperativen Komplikationsrate korreliert. Der Erhalt respektive die Steigerung der präoperativen körperlichen Leistungsreserven kann das Risiko für postoperative Komplikationen signifikant reduzieren.

interventions.name:
Biweekly clinical and laboratory monitoring, close monitoring of the nutritional status, nutritional interventions if indicated, regular outpatient physiotherapy.

Summary of the study's laboratory protocol:

Biweekly monitoring: CHE, CRP (inflammation check), and complete blood count (CBC).

The control patients represent the previous standard of care. To avoid bias, they will meet the exact same inclusion criteria as the intervention group. Their data will be retrospectively extracted from the hospital information system

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Histologically confirmed malignancy of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract.
Indication for neoadjuvant therapy (chemotherapy/radiochemotherapy).
Planned curative resection.
Exclusion criteria:
Age under 18 years. (Alternativ: Age < 18 years)
No planned neoadjuvant therapy.
Lack of capacity to consent or lack of informed consent to participate.
